::: {#thm-standardized-mean-sd}
#### Standardized values have mean 0 and standard deviation 1

For $n \ge 2$ observations with $s > 0$,
the [standardized values](#def-standardization) $\dsn{z}$
have sample mean $0$ and sample standard deviation $1$.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

Stated for the standardized Caravan variables in @james2021islr2e [sec. 4.7.6, p. 183];
the proof is the elementary calculation.
:::

:::

::: proof

The sample mean of the $z_i$ is
$$
\ba
\avgin \frac{x_i - \bar x}{s}
&= \frac{1}{s} \paren{\avgin x_i - \bar x}\\
&= \frac{1}{s} (\bar x - \bar x)\\
&= 0.
\ea
$$
Since the mean of the $z_i$ is $0$,
their sample variance is
$$
\ba
\frac{1}{n-1} \sumin z_i^2
&= \frac{1}{s^2} \cdot \frac{1}{n-1} \sumin (x_i - \bar x)^2\\
&= \frac{s^2}{s^2}\\
&= 1,
\ea
$$
so their sample standard deviation is $\sqrt{1} = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-scale-wcgs}
#### Standardizing cholesterol in R

In R, `scale()` returns the standardized values of a column,
as a one-column matrix.
For the WCGS cholesterol values:

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
z <- scale(wcgs$chol)[, 1]
mean(z, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(z, na.rm = TRUE)
```

The mean is $0$ up to rounding error, and the standard deviation is $1$,
as @thm-standardized-mean-sd says.
The `na.rm = TRUE` is needed because `r sum(is.na(wcgs$chol))` of the cholesterol values are missing.

:::
